_about: A few names whose page needs words of its own beyond the data (design 3.2: Jesus and Immanuel, written with reverence). 'text' is shown under the opening paragraph; 'links' are site addresses. Scripture quoted here is the Berean Standard Bible.

Jesus.text: Jesus is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, and the angel gave the reason for it: “He will save His people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21). Out of reverence it is rarely given to children in English-speaking families, while in Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking families Jesús is a common name. This page lists the name; the story of Jesus himself is told in the Gospels.

Immanuel.text: Immanuel is the name Isaiah gave in prophecy (Isaiah 7:14), and Matthew explains it: “God with us” (Matthew 1:23). It is given to children today, most often spelled Emmanuel.
